name: research
description: Research skills for reading the web well: deep-research convenes a multi-vendor council (the user's logged-in ChatGPT and Gemini, cross-examined anonymously) and writes a chairman's brief with verified sources; read-twitter reads one X post with its thread, replies, quoted post, images, video and linked material; fetch-web-sources reaches docs pages, code and repositories a plain fetch cannot see; watch-video extracts what a video says and shows; link-rot-checker decides which links in a batch are alive, dead or unknown.

interface.shortDescription: Research councils, X posts, and the web, code and video a fetcher can't see
interface.longDescription: Research skills for the yystack marketplace. deep-research poses one question to the user's own logged-in ChatGPT and Gemini web UIs, cross-examines their answers anonymously, and writes a chairman's brief with every load-bearing citation verified — proposing the council before spending paid quotas. read-twitter reads one X/Twitter post through a logged-in browser: body, self-thread, notable replies, quoted post, images read as pixels, native video, and the real content behind each t.co link. fetch-web-sources is a ladder of cheap, credential-free recipes for when a fetch comes back empty or 404: find the real docs path in llms.txt, ask for the markdown twin, search code and issues without a GitHub token, take an uptake census of a new product, and research an open-source deployment behind a login from its own public issues and docs. watch-video extracts content from a video — offline with ffmpeg and whisper.cpp for a local file, or through Gemini for YouTube, optionally saving a timestamped knowledge file to answer follow-ups from. link-rot-checker classifies a batch of links as alive, dead or unknown, demanding a positive marker for each verdict and a made-up-id control.
defaultPrompt: Deep-research this decision with ChatGPT and Gemini and give me a brief.
Read this X thread and the links in it.
This docs page comes back empty — get me its content.
Find every public repository that contains this exact string.
Summarise this YouTube talk and extract the steps.
